kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-02.title: Go round the circle
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-02.body:
Going left from Yana, Xena is 4 places away; going right, she is 7 places away. Walking 4 places one way and then 7 more places (from Xena back to Yana the other way round) takes us once round the circle: $4 + 7 = 11$ girls.

**Answer: (C) 11**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-02.title: Count the girls in between
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-02.body:
On one side there are 3 girls between Yana and Xena, on the other side 6. Together with Yana and Xena: $3 + 6 + 2 = 11$.

**Answer: (C) 11**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-03.title: One of them is 0
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-03.body:
If all 2017 numbers were at least 1, their sum would be at least 2017. The sum is only 2016, so at least one number is 0, and then the product is 0.

**Answer: (E) 0**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-09.title: Pair up the houses
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-09.body:
Group the houses as (1,2), (3,4), (5,6), (7,8) and house 9 on its own. Each pair of neighbours has at most 10 people: at most 40. House 9 has a neighbour (house 8) with at least 2 people, so house 9 has at most 8. Total at most $40 + 8 = 48$.

This is possible: 8, 2, 8, 2, 8, 2, 8, 2, 8 (every pair of neighbours has exactly 10, and $5 \cdot 8 + 4 \cdot 2 = 48$).

**Answer: (C) 48**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-18.title: Add up the detentions
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-18.body:
9 hours 10 minutes $= 550$ minutes $= 10 \times 55$. After being late $n$ times, Simon has spent $10(1 + 2 + \dots + n)$ minutes, so $1 + 2 + \dots + n = 55$. Since $1 + 2 + \dots + 10 = 55$, he was late 10 times.

**Answer: (C) 10**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-18.title: Running total
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-18.body:
Totals in minutes: 10, 30, 60, 100, 150, 210, 280, 360, 450, 550 — the 10th late arrival brings it to 550 minutes.

**Answer: (C) 10**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-19.title: Equation
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-19.body:
Let Dana be $x$ years old now. Then $x + 16 = 5(x - 4)$, so $x + 16 = 5x - 20$, $4x = 36$, $x = 9$. She turns 16 in $16 - 9 = 7$ years.

**Answer: (B) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-19.title: Think in gaps
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-19.body:
The time between "four years ago" and "in 16 years" is 20 years. Her age then is 5 times her age four years ago, so the difference, 20 years, is 4 times her age four years ago: she was 5, so now she is 9 and turns 16 in 7 years.

**Answer: (B) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-24.title: Estimate with a cube root
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-24.body:
The product is $8 \cdot 27 \cdot 91 = 19656$. Three consecutive numbers have a product close to the cube of the middle one, and $27^3 = 19683$, so try $26 \cdot 27 \cdot 28$: $26 = 2 \cdot 13$, $27 = 3^3$, $28 = 2^2 \cdot 7$, product $2^3 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 7 \cdot 13$ ✓.

Sum $26 + 27 + 28 = 81$.

**Answer: (C) 81**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-24.title: Group the prime factors
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-24.body:
One number must contain the factor 13 and one the factor 7; with $3^3 = 27$ in the middle, 26 and 28 are its neighbours, and indeed $26 \cdot 27 \cdot 28$ uses exactly the factors $2 \cdot 13$, $3^3$, $2^2 \cdot 7$. Sum 81.

**Answer: (C) 81**

kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-27.title: Compare with one third
kangaroo-ca-2017-g0708-27.body:
Among $1, \dots, N$ there are $\lfloor N/3 \rfloor$ multiples of 3, which is always more than $\frac{N}{3} - 1$. We need it to equal $0.3N$, which must be a whole number, so $N$ is a multiple of 10: $N = 10k$, and we need $\lfloor 10k/3 \rfloor = 3k$.

The number $\frac{10k}{3}$ lies between $3k$ and $3k+1$ exactly when $\frac{k}{3} < 1$, i.e. $k = 1$ or $2$.

- $N = 10$: multiples 3, 6, 9 — 3 of 10 = 30% ✓
- $N = 20$: 6 of 20 = 30% ✓
- $N = 30$: 10 of 30 — too many, and for larger $N$ the share gets closer to $33\frac13\%$.

So there are 2 such numbers.

**Answer: (C) 2**
